But adjacency diagonally: queens in consecutive rows cannot be in columns differing by 1. Also queens in same row or column can't be adjacent anyway. So rule reduces to: For any two queens in rows r and r+1, columns cannot differ by 1. Also for rows r and r+2? They can share a long diagonal? The rule says: "Queens separated by more than one row MAY share a long diagonal; this is not the ordinary chess N-queens diagonal rule." So only adjacency diagonally between consecutive rows is forbidden. So we just need to avoid columns difference 1 for consecutive rows.
